The narrator has a distinctive psychological depth: their former inventory work, unemployment, loneliness, and obsessive attention to objects shape their increasingly personal involvement. The couple gains texture through small, convincing habits—sharing the bag, adjusting the umbrella, misplacing keys—and their mixture of tenderness and irritation makes them more than vehicles for the uncanny mystery. Brief figures such as the cyclist and the sister remain appropriately peripheral while grounding the narrator’s experience in ordinary concern.
